# Skills For Real Engineers [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/mattpocock/skills)](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter) ## Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. ### 1. Get the skills
Claude Code ```bash claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ``` Updates itself by default.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Updates itself at startup.
GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } ``` In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.
Gemini CLI (manual updates) ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity ``` Re-run both commands to update.
Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) ```bash npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose ``` When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.
### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: - Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) - Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels) - Ask you where you want to save any docs we create ### 3. Bam - you're ready to go. ## Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. ### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want > "No-one knows exactly what they want" > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. **The Fix** is to use: - [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses - [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change. ### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose > With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. > > Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215) **The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. **The Fix** for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.
Example Here's an example [glossary](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/blob/076a5a7a182db0fe1e62971dd7a68bcadf010f1c/CONTEXT.md) (still named `CONTEXT.md` at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my `course-video-manager` repo. Which one is easier to read? - **BEFORE**: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" - **AFTER**: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session.
This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md). It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. > [!TIP] > A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: > > - **Variables, functions and files are named consistently**, using the shared language > - As a result, the **codebase is easier to navigate** for the agent > - The agent also **spends fewer tokens on thinking**, because it has access to a more concise language ### #3: The Code Doesn't Work > "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent _still_ produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. **The Fix**: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a **[`/tdd`](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) skill** you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a **[`/diagnosing-bugs`](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)** skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. ### #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud > "Invest in the design of the system _every day_." > > Kent Beck, [Extreme Programming Explained](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Extreme-Programming-Explained-Embrace-Change/dp/0321278658) > "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." > > John Ousterhout, [A Philosophy Of Software Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Philosophy-Software-Design-2nd/dp/173210221X) **The Problem**: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. **The Fix** for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: - [`/to-spec`](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md) quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, [`/improve-codebase-architecture`](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md) surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. ### Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. ## Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. **User-invoked** skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. `/grill-me`); their job is to orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills can be invoked by you _or_ reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one. ### Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. **User-invoked** - **[ask-matt](./skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md)**: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo. - **[grill-with-docs](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md)**: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[triage](./skills/engineering/triage/SKILL.md)**: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. - **[setup-matt-pocock-skills](./skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md)**: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills. - **[to-spec](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md)**: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed. - **[to-tickets](./skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md)**: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker. - **[implement](./skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md)**: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing. - **[implement-spec](./skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md)**: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. # Orkas **An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the **Commander** what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent** — to work on it together. Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A **project** holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. **To-dos** split the work between people and agents, **Auto-advance** lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and **scheduled automations** repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business. **[⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an **Orkas API Key** in **Settings → Models**, then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings. --- ## Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents **Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode**, and the personal agents **OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent**. The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way. [Using Claude Code and Codex together →](https://orkas.ai/blog/claude-code-codex-together/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Why Orkas - **A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest** — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit. - **Local-first by design** — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

--- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`. Install with a single command: ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 7 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 7. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/claude-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Browse the [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/showcase) for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix. - Product launch videos and feature announcements - PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions - Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations - Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music - Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers - Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines ## Frame.md **frame.md — your design system, ready for video.** Every brand has a `design.md`. None of them were written for a camera. `frame.md` is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome. The output is a `DESIGN.md` superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

details.readme:
Make the scene first. Then make it a video.
Open source previs in a browser tab: block the set, move the cast, cut the camera, hand the shot to an AI video model.

Try it in the browser · Quick start · Guide for AI agents · Docs · Changelog · Discord

Top: the greybox blocked in CozyClay. Bottom: the AI video made from it. Same idea, a parkour jump: the blocking holds the timing and the camera.
## Why AI video costs money per take, and one miss means paying again. A text prompt cannot hold a whole scene: where everyone stands, how they move, where the camera is, when it cuts. CozyClay lets you make those decisions first, in 3D, where they are cheap to change. Then the video model gets the shot as a first frame, a greybox reference clip and a prompt that describes the real framing. It follows the blocking instead of guessing. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["Stage
set + cast"] --> M["Motion
compiled + QA"] --> C["Camera
shots + cuts"] --> E["Export
frame · clip · prompt"] --> V["AI video model"] ``` ## Quick start ```bash npx cozyclay ``` That is the whole install. You need Node.js 22.19 or newer and a Chromium browser. You do not need a GPU, Python or a model download. The studio opens at `http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/`. **Updating.** `npx cozyclay` fetches the newest release each time you run it. After `npm install -g cozyclay`, the studio shows a small **Update** chip in the top bar when a newer release is out. **Update now** installs it, and **Restart now** starts the new version in the same terminal; the studio reloads once your project is saved. On Windows the chip gives you the command to copy instead: one-click stays off there by design. `cclay update` does the same from the terminal. `--no-update-check` or `COZYCLAY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns the check off for one launch; `cclay update --off` turns it off for good, and `cclay update --on` brings it back. > **Asking an AI agent to set it up?** Give it this repository link. Its instructions are in > [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md). ## What you can do | | | | --- | --- | | **Stage** | Build the set from primitives. Add rigged characters, or capsule stand-ins when nobody needs to move a limb. Fly the view like a 3D editor. | | **Move** | Describe the action. The agent writes a motion spec, and a deterministic compiler in the browser bakes every frame. QA checks collisions, foot slide, reach and hand contact before you see it. | | **Shoot** | Put shots on a timeline, draw dolly rails, look through the lens. Each shot knows the limits of the video model you target. | | **Export** | Keyframe pack (first and last frame, greybox clip, camera, prompt), mp4, depth and normal passes, contact sheet, OTIO cut list. | | **Storyboard** | Prefer stills? A Storyboard project is a row of panels with captions, an animatic and a contact sheet. | | **Undo anything** | Every edit, including each change the agent makes, is one undo step. | ## Direct it with AI The same scene can be driven from three places, live, while you watch the viewport. | Surface | Start | For | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent panel** | `Cmd/Ctrl+B` in the studio | Chat in the studio. Sign in with ChatGPT or use your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, MiniMax, OpenRouter, CLIProxyAPI). | | **MCP server** | `npx -y cozyclay mcp` | Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client. | | **Terminal** | `cclay live status --wait` | Coding agents that drive a running studio, JSON in and out. | ```json { "mcpServers": { "cozyclay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "cozyclay", "mcp"] } } } ``` ## From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/NomaDamas/CozyClay.git && cd CozyClay npm install npm run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/ npm test ``` ## Docs | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) | Install, run and connect, written for AI agents | | [`docs/motion3-agent-guide.md`](docs/motion3-agent-guide.md) | Motion specs, compile and QA | | [`docs/agent-cli.md`](docs/agent-cli.md) | `cclay live`, model providers, sessions | | [`mcp/README.md`](mcp/README.md) | MCP tools and the live protocol | | [`docs/studio-ui-ia.md`](docs/studio-ui-ia.md) | Every control and where it lives | | [`docs/privacy.md`](docs/privacy.md) | Anonymous telemetry and how to turn it off (`cclay telemetry off`) | | [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) | Contribution rules | ## Guides | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [Greybox to AI video](https://cozyclay.org/greybox-to-video/) | Why a grey blockout is the most reliable input for a video model, and the block-then-generate loop | | [Previs software compared](https://cozyclay.org/previs-software/) | Free, open source and browser-based previs tools side by side | | [Seedance 2.5 camera control](https://cozyclay.org/seedance-camera-control/) | Getting the same camera on every take with a reference clip | | [Camera control for AI video](https://cozyclay.org/ai-camera-control/) | Why camera prompts drift and what the models actually accept | Found a bug or want a feature? Website · Download · Documentation · Release notes · Roadmap · Project status · Contributing

# Horizon Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten in Rust. Same worlds, same rules, same terrain, checked against the Java game by more than 300 differential harnesses. Free, open source and unofficial. > Not an official Minecraft product, nor approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data: you need your own copy of Java Edition 26.3. ## Download Get **the Horizon launcher** from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev) or [the launcher releases](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/releases?q=launcher-v&expanded=true) (Linux x86-64, macOS on Apple Silicon, macOS on Intel from the next Nightly, Windows x64). It installs and updates the game, prepares its files from your copy of Minecraft, and updates itself. **You need** a Microsoft account that owns Java Edition ([why](docs/microsoft-account.md)) and a GPU with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 (Linux), Vulkan or DirectX 12 (Windows), or a Mac (Apple Silicon, or Intel from the next Nightly). An existing Minecraft install (official launcher, Prism, MultiMC...) is reused; without one, Play downloads 26.3 from Mojang for your account. Step by step: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## What works today - **The game:** vanilla world generation, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book, on vanilla saves. Worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded. [Status](#project-status). - **Extras:** new menus, graphics presets, distant terrain up to 1024 chunks, controllers, zoom, minimap and more, off by default where they change the vanilla look. [Settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings). - **Packs:** resource packs, and data packs with functions, predicates, item modifiers and world generation. - **Multiplayer:** invite friends with a code, Open to LAN, join servers (online mode included). [Multiplayer](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/multiplayer). - **Mods:** content mods (blocks, items, data) and native Rust mods, built by the launcher with nothing to install. Java mod jars do not run. [Mods](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods). In the Rust client, with vanilla assets and no mods or shaders:
## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a server, and invites friends over Tailscale. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command and needs no Java. [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Modpacks The launcher imports Modrinth and CurseForge packs and plays the mods Horizon can carry over: today, content mods made of data and assets, not Java code. [Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped with the game, reads its state as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands over MCP. ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until done and reply with the result; `horizon-ctl help` lists them all. [Agent control](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source Needs Rust 1.90+, Python 3.10+, JDK 25, and on Linux `libasound2-dev libudev-dev`. `horizon-prepare` builds the game's resources from **your own copy** of Java Edition 26.3 (checked against `research-lock.json`) and never downloads it: 1. **Client:** play 26.3 once in the official launcher. Horizon reads `~/.minecraft` (or `--minecraft-dir` / `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`). 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar (`downloads.server.url` in `versions/26.3/26.3.json`), passed once with `--server-jar` or `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Prepared files land in the gitignored `.local/`: never commit or share them. Options, controls and architecture: [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md); all developer docs: [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Roadmap What is in progress, what comes next and where to help: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), or [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) with the work board and what shipped. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) (vanilla first, small pull requests). Questions: [Discord](https://discord.gg/playhorizon). Before a pull request, run the self-check and paste its output: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy, the touched crates' tests, the Python tests, the public-tree check and the vanilla harnesses your change affects. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources. ## Project status **Player-visible gaps: 833 open** of the 833 the [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) found, reading every vanilla 26.3 method against Horizon's code: vanilla behaviour a player would notice that Horizon doesn't have yet. By area: Screens, HUD and client packets [197](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3518); Entity and block rendering, models [129](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3519); Animals [110](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3512); Server and players on the server [106](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3520); Blocks, redstone and fluids [86](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3516); Entities, projectiles, vehicles and decorations [64](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3514); Monsters and bosses [53](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3513); Mob AI, villagers and raids [35](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3521); World, world generation and saves [32](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3517); Items, enchantments and inventories [21](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3515). This number goes down as gaps close (`tools/parity_gaps.py`); the harness results below say that what is tested matches. The table is the project's own audit: every subsystem matches vanilla in every harness that compares it. 100% means 100% of what the harnesses compare, not that nothing else differs. ### Java parity: 100% Scores: 0 (absent), 0.25 (started), 0.5 (playable, major features missing), 0.75 (mostly complete) or 1 (complete and verified by differential tests); the percentage is their average. Last audited 2026-10-13: all 281 harnesses pass on Linux and macOS. The [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) adds a method-by-method view of what is ported. | Subsystem | Score | Main gaps | | --- | ---: | --- | | Window, input and game loop | 1 | None: game loop, options, camera, auto-jump, toggle sprint/sneak and frame limiter match | | Assets and resources | 1 | None: item models match over 196,290 stacks; the resource pack screen over 3,000 sessions | | Network protocol and multiplayer | 1 | None: joins vanilla servers; the dedicated server matches vanilla's files, login, configuration, play and command tree; details.readme:
AudioSmith

A voice studio that runs on your Mac.
Speech, voices, stories, audiobooks, dubbing, transcription and dictation, on Apple silicon.

Website · Download · Changelog

English · 简体中文

AudioSmith turns text into speech, clones and designs voices, gives a story a cast, reads a book into an M4B, dubs a video into another language, transcribes a recording with who said what, and types what you say into any app. Every model runs on your Mac's GPU with [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx): no account, no cloud service, no Python. It runs on your Mac, and once its models are downloaded it works offline. [Features](#features) · [Install](#install) · [Models](#models) · [Privacy](#privacy) · [Build from source](#build-from-source) · [Licence](#licence-and-credits) > **The current version, 0.4.0-beta.7, is a beta.** Releases are signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple and update themselves. Expect rough edges; see [Known limits](#known-limits) and [the changelog](https://actnow.dev/audiosmith/changelog). ## Features ### Studio - **Write or import** a script (TXT, MD, DOCX, EPUB, SRT, VTT). Markup adds pauses (`[pause 400ms]`), pace (`[slow]`, `[fast]`), emphasis, spelling and one-off pronunciations (`[[word|say]]`). - **Pick a model by what it is for:** Standard voices, Fast clone, High-fidelity clone, Voice design, Fast English voices, English clone or Multilingual all-rounder. The technical name is one click away. - **Few controls:** the model, one Voice list and the speed. Everything else is under Advanced, filled with settings measured for each model. - **Long scripts** render in chunks and play while they render. Text you did not change comes from a cache. - **Export audio:** WAV or M4A, and MP3, FLAC or Opus with ffmpeg. Even out the loudness to −16, −18 or −23 LUFS, trim the silence, add tags, save the script and subtitles beside it. ### Voices | Discover voices | My voices | |---|---| | | | - **Discover** 37 chosen voices, mostly Chinese and English: designed voices whose reference ships with the app, ready to speak at once, and the best built-in speakers. Preview them and save the ones you like. - **Clone** a voice from a recording or from any audio or video file. AudioSmith picks the best stretch and transcribes it. A recorded consent statement marks a voice as your own. - **Checked references:** every reference is rated (good, fine, needs work) with a tip or two, and cleaned: noise removed only when there is some, silence trimmed, loudness evened out. The original is kept. - **Design** a voice from a sentence in English or Chinese ("a warm narrator in her thirties, calm and clear"), or start from one of eight presets. - **Hear before you pick:** every voice list (Studio, Stories, Audiobook, Dub) has a ▶ on each voice: built-in speakers play a short bundled sample, even before their model is downloaded; your own voices play their sample. - **Portable voices:** a model's built-in speaker or a designed voice can be turned into a clone that every cloning model can speak with. It sounds close to the original, not the same, and says so. - **Deleting a voice** says where it is used, and Undo in the toast brings it back for about 10 seconds. - Voices are `.asvoice` files you can share. VoiceStudio's `.ovsvoice` files import too. ### Stories - **Write `Name: line`** and AudioSmith casts the characters. Stage directions such as `MOM (softly):` become the line's direction instead of being read out. - **Dialogue that flows:** the gaps follow the conversation (Dialogue, Reading or Relaxed). A character's consecutive lines are said in one go, and each voice is brought to one loudness. - **AI director:** the writing assistant (Qwen3 4B, on this Mac) reads the whole story and gives each line one of 13 emotions with a strength, kept coherent across the scene; you can change any of them. Models that take instructions hear them; the others read the lines as written, and the page says so. - **Whole dialogue:** a dialogue model speaks the characters' lines a scene at a time, so each line answers the one before it. *Dialogue · Light* (SoulX-Podcast) needs 16 GB of memory, *Dialogue · One take* (MOSS-TTSD) 24 GB. Narration stays on the story's model. - Export a WAV, an M4B, or one stem per character. ### Audiobook - **Import** an EPUB, TXT, Markdown or DOCX book. Chapters come from its headings. - **Dialogue passages:** mark a scene with `[dialogue]` … `[/dialogue]` (`[对话]` in Chinese) and one `Name: line` per turn, and a dialogue model speaks it with the characters answering each other. Without the model the passage is read line by line. - **Loudness** per chapter for ACX (Audible) or podcasts. A read-along player follows the text. - **Export** an M4B with chapters, cover and tags, a cue sheet, or one file per chapter. - **Resume** after quitting. After an edit, only the changed lines are rendered again. ### Dub - **Drop in a video or audio file,** or paste a link (yt-dlp, which you turn on). Before anything downloads, the page shows the cover, the site, the title and the length, then the download's real progress. New dubs are made in Chinese; when the video is already Chinese they switch to English. Add more languages as you like. - **Four steps:** 1. Separate the voices from the background (HTDemucs). 2. Transcribe and tell the speakers apart (Transcription with speakers, or Qwen3-ASR with Sortformer). 3. Translate with the local writing assistant, Ollama, a cloud model, DeepL, Google or Microsoft. A glossary keeps names right. 4. Speak each line in its speaker's cloned voice, fitted to the original timing, also from another language (a Japanese speaker speaking Chinese). Such lines are heard again: one in the wrong language or with the wrong words is made again, or marked Listen. - **Conversations recorded together:** for dubs into Chinese or English with two speakers or more, *Dialogue · Light* records each conversation as a whole, so answers sound like answers, then fits every line to its time. On by default for new dubs; needs 16 GB of memory. - **Edit** lines on a timeline (pinch or ⌘ with the wheel to zoom, swipe to pan), compare A/B, preview the video, and re-dub only what changed. A 2-hour video with 2,000 lines stays quick. - **Export** an MP4 with one audio track per language and soft subtitles, or M4A, WAV, SRT, VTT, ASS and stems. Batch dubs a whole folder, and can watch one. ### Transcribe and dictation - **Transcribe** recordings and videos with word timings. Qwen3-ASR handles Chinese, English and 28 more languages; Whisper covers the rest and translates speech into English. - **Transcription with speakers** says who says what (S1, S2…) in one pass; click a speaker to name it. Copy, TXT, SRT, VTT and JSON exports carry the names. - **Dictation anywhere:** press ⌘⇧Space in any app, speak, and the text is typed where your cursor is, about 0.2–0.3 s after you stop. Your clipboard is kept. A menu bar icon, a small pill and sounds you can choose show when it listens. ### Workflows and batch - **Workflows:** chain steps on a canvas (sources, speak, transcribe, translate, convert, even out, condition, export), start from a template, and run them over up to 50 inputs. A run continues after a restart. - **Batch** queues dubs and watches a folder. ### For agents and scripts - **OpenAI-compatible API** on `http://127.0.0.1:3901/v1`: speech, transcriptions, translations, models and voices. Point any OpenAI SDK at it. - **AudioSmith's own API** (`/api`) drives every page: voices, stories, audiobooks, dubs, batch, workflows, exports. Jobs report progress over SSE, and `/ws/tts` streams speech. - **MCP server** over HTTP (`/mcp`) and stdio (`AudioSmith --mcp-stdio`), with 33 tools. Deleting needs `confirm: true`; cloning needs consent and works only from this Mac (or with the API key). - **Integrations page:** one prompt sets up Claude Code, Codex or Cursor (server and agent skill); there are snippets for n8n, curl, Python, JavaScript and the OpenAI Agents SDK. ```sh curl http://127.0.0.1:3901/v1/audio/speech \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "tts-1", "voice": "alloy", "input": "Build finished. All tests passed."}' \ -o speech.wav ``` The full reference is [docs/local-api.md](docs/local-api.md), and `/docs` in the running app. ### And more - **Tools:** compare voices A/B, speak a recording again in another voice, fit text to a duration, probe a file, check a watermark. - **Invisible watermark:** generated audio carries an AudioSeal mark, on by default (Settings → Privacy), and Tools can detect it. - **Calls:** an AI phone agent on your own Twilio account. It always says it is an AI, and uses only designed or consented voices. Off until you set it up. - **The app:** a sidebar with search (⌘F) and sections that fold; what is running shows as cards at its foot, and the Tasks page lists every job. Projects and History libraries, one job queue that resumes after a restart, the command palette (⌘K), ⌘1–9 for the main pages, light and dark themes, English and 简体中文. - **Memory:** models you have not used for 30 minutes are unloaded (Settings → Models & network → Memory) and load again when needed. ## Install **Requirements** - macOS 15 or later, on Apple silicon (M1 or later). - Memory: 8 GB runs the Fast pack; 16 GB is recommended, and needed for *Dialogue · Light*; 24 GB runs the Quality pack (high-fidelity cloning, voice design, dubbing and the writing assistant) and *Dialogue · One take*. - Disk: 1.3–17 GB for models, depending on the pack; the dialogue models add 2.4 GB and 10.9 GB. **Steps** 1. details.readme:
html-anime

Prompt an anime. Your coding agent draws it in code.

A still from Kokuyō, drawn entirely in HTML. Watch it on the site · media/film.mp4

An anime, written as HTML. You write a scene. [The site](https://blixvip.github.io/html-anime/) turns it into a shot sheet: holds, one expensive shot, a closed color script. Paste that sheet into Claude, Codex, Cursor, or Grok. The agent draws the frames. The pictures are HTML, timed for [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes). Nothing here calls a video model. ## The film Kokuyō. Watch it on [the site](https://blixvip.github.io/html-anime/) or open [media/film.mp4](media/film.mp4).
## Start ``` git clone https://github.com/blixvip/html-anime.git cd html-anime ``` Open the folder in the agent you already use and paste a sheet as the first message. The site builds the sheet in the browser. `harness/compile.js` builds the same sheet in Node. Serve the site from this folder, then open the address it prints: ``` python -m http.server ``` Opening `index.html` as a file shows that same instruction. The sheet will not run until the folder is served. Or build a sheet in Node (no dependencies): ```js import { compileBrief } from "./harness/compile.js"; const sheet = compileBrief({ logline: "On a roof in the rain, a red moon opens and a line of light falls.", seconds: 8, // 8, 12, or 20 aspect: "16:9", // or "9:16" script: "indigo", // indigo, eclipse, noon, or festival dialogue: "The rain hid the sound of the blade.", }); console.log(sheet.ok ? sheet.markdown : sheet.error); ``` | Agent | What it reads | Open | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` | `claude` | | Codex | `AGENTS.md` | `codex` | | Cursor | `.cursor/rules/html-anime.mdc` | `cursor .` | | Grok | `AGENTS.md` | `grok` | ## What is in the repo - `index.html` — the site - `skills/html-anime-direct/SKILL.md` — which shots exist - `skills/html-anime-cel/SKILL.md` — how a frame is painted - `skills/html-anime-timing/SKILL.md` — twos, holds, the smear - `skills/html-anime-camera/SKILL.md` — the cut and the frame - `skills/html-anime-render/SKILL.md` — the HyperFrames file - `harness/compile.js` — logline to sheet - `media/film.mp4` — Kokuyō, the film - `media/city.jpg`, `media/moon.jpg`, `media/fight.jpg`, `media/helm.jpg`, `media/ren.jpg` — stills from it - `films/roof/` — an 8 second reference. File shape and the color-dip cut, not a film to remix - `AGENTS.md` — the contract ## Test ``` npm test ``` Checks that every runtime sums exactly and has one sakuga shot, and that the sheet carries the size, frame count, and dialogue. ## Render the reference ``` cd films/roof npx hyperframes preview ``` Lint before you trust a new film: ``` npx hyperframes lint npx hyperframes validate ``` ## Sheet rules the agent is not allowed to break - Shot times sum to 8, 12, or 20 seconds - One sakuga shot. The others stay on three drawings - Acting on twos. Rain and a blade on ones - Only the hexes printed on the sheet - The line you wrote, verbatim, or no dialogue at all ## Community 💬 [Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/zEB4VjmfSb) for questions, help, feedback, and updates. ## More from blixvip | Project | What it does | | --- | --- | | **[GenMotion](https://github.com/blixvip/GenMotion)** | Type an idea, get a finished motion-graphics video. Top Western + Chinese image models, your own API keys. | | **[NullMotion](https://github.com/blixvip/NullMotion)** | Play a finished motion-graphics ad in sync with the rough drafts it grew from. Export the breakdown as MP4. | | **[MotionClone](https://github.com/blixvip/MotionClone)** | Rebuild any reference video as an editable HyperFrames project and compare it against the original. | | **[easyedit](https://github.com/blixvip/easyedit)** | Type a movie name, get a fan edit: captioned speech cut, then a montage cut to the beat. | | **[stick](https://github.com/blixvip/stick)** | Free, open-source stick figure animation software for Windows, Linux and the web. | | **[thumbnail-studio](https://github.com/blixvip/thumbnail-studio)** | A minimal Windows workspace for YouTube thumbnails: ChatGPT beside your references. | | **[blixtrade](https://github.com/blixvip/blixtrade)** | Open-source core of BLIX, the AI memecoin terminal for Solana, with a public API and MCP server. | If one of these helped you, a ⭐ helps other people find it. Follow [@waselyyy](https://x.com/waselyyy) for new drops. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). The reference film's font keeps its own license: see [films/roof/fonts/NOTICE.txt](films/roof/fonts/NOTICE.txt).
